youtube_title: Why Every Giveaway Says 'No Purchase Necessary' 🦝⚖️
caption: A lottery generally combines a prize, chance and payment. The FTC says purchase-required sweepstakes are illegal in the U.S. — which is why giveaways offer free entry. State rules still apply.
script: Every giveaway says no purchase necessary, because without it, it might be an illegal lottery. [disclaimer] Here's the secret. In America, lawyers say a lottery has three parts. A prize. Luck. And paying to play. And private lotteries are generally illegal! So how can a soda company run a giveaway where winners are picked by luck? Easy. They take out the paying part! The Federal Trade Commission says contests like this that make you buy something are illegal in the United States. It says real sweepstakes are free, and winning is by chance. And sweepstakes mail has to say you don't have to pay to enter. That's why every giveaway has a free way in, like an online form or mailing in a card. It kills the paying part! But no purchase necessary isn't a magic spell. The free way has to be real. Each state has its own rules, and some need extra fine print, a license, or even a bond. Other agencies, like the Post Office and the FCC, also go after shady prize games. And skill contests are a whole different thing. So just printing three words on a box doesn't make any game legal. [loop] So the next time you see no purchase necessary in tiny print, remember
